title: Arabic Catering Dubai: plan the menu and service
focus: Arabic food catering in Dubai can be a mezze reception, a shared family meal or a staffed buffet. Choose the regional dishes first, then the portions and service format. A majlis table, wedding reception and office lunch need different timing, space and staffing; your proposal brings those details together.

sections.title: Choose a regional direction before expanding the selection
paragraphs: For a Levantine direction, discuss hummus, moutabal, tabbouleh, fattoush, stuffed vine leaves and flatbread, followed by shish taouk or lamb kofta. An Emirati brief may centre on machboos, harees or another family favourite. Tell us the dishes and preparations your guests expect so the menu has a clear identity.

An ouzi or whole-lamb centrepiece needs a plan for carving, rice, accompaniments and service. A grill-led evening needs suitable cooking space and venue permission. We review the kitchen and guest count before recommending the equipment and chef team.

Halal sourcing is part of the menu discussion. Share any required documentation, allergies and ingredient exclusions at the start. We confirm the proposed ingredients and preparation arrangements before you approve the menu.

sections.title: Give the menu a clear direction
paragraphs: Build an Arabic catering menu in Dubai as a complete meal: cold mezze and salads, warm starters, a grill or rice centrepiece, breads and a sweet finish. Choose enough variety for your guests without repeating the same rich flavours across every course.

For a majlis gathering or family dinner, shared platters can be served in a sequence. For a wedding or office event, a buffet may give guests more flexibility. Discuss whether starters are a welcome before dinner or the main food for a standing reception; the portion plan changes with that choice.

Your Arabic catering cost per person in Dubai depends on the final dishes, adult and child counts, service hours, staffing and equipment. Request a written menu with food, team, tableware, delivery and VAT identified so you can compare the complete proposal.

sections.title: Keep the buffet easy to approach and enjoy
paragraphs: A buffet works best when guests can see the choices and move through the serving area comfortably. Think about where the queue may form, how plates will be collected and whether guests need access from one side or several points. The layout should suit the room rather than force everyone towards one crowded corner.

Keep breads, sauces and salads close to the dishes they accompany. Confirm how hot rice and grilled dishes will be replenished, and whether a live grill or carving station needs its own chef. Dietary labels and separate serving utensils are agreed as part of the service plan.

The venue needs enough space for both guests and staff to move. A beautiful display is only useful if it can be maintained without interrupting the event. Confirm the equipment, station staffing and clear-down responsibilities in the proposal so the buffet remains a working service area as well as a visual centrepiece.
